back: Sorted set: ZADD / ZINCRBY to update, ZRANGE key 0 9 REV WITHSCORES for the top 10, ZREVRANK for a rank.

front: Hash vs string-of-JSON for an object?
back: A hash lets you read or update one field (HGET, HINCRBY) without rewriting the whole value.
LPUSH the new item, then LTRIM key 0 N-1 to keep only the latest N.
Approximate distinct count in at most 12 KB with ~0.81% standard error. PFADD, PFCOUNT, PFMERGE.

front: Stream vs list as a queue?
back: Streams keep entries after reading, have consumer groups and XACK, and support replay. A popped list item is gone.
Seconds remaining; -1 = no expiry; -2 = key doesn't exist.

front: What clears a key's TTL by accident?
back: Overwriting it with a plain SET. Use SET ... EX again or SET ... KEEPTTL.
Lazily when a key is accessed, plus a background cycle that samples keys with TTLs and deletes expired ones.
Point-in-time snapshot written by a forked child using copy-on-write. Compact and fast to load; loses writes since the last snapshot.
always (safest, slowest), everysec (default, lose ~1 s), no (OS decides, least safe).
Asynchronous: acknowledged writes can be lost on failover. WAIT narrows but doesn't close the window.

front: How does Redis Cluster place keys?
back: 16,384 hash slots; slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384; each primary owns a range of slots.
Only the part in braces is hashed, so {user:42}:cart and {user:42}:profile share a slot and can be used together.
MOVED: the slot lives elsewhere, update your map. ASK: during migration, send this one request to the new node.
Every command is atomic, but one slow O(N) command (KEYS, huge HGETALL, long Lua) blocks every client.

front: What do Redis 6 I/O threads do?
back: Read requests and write replies on sockets in parallel; commands still execute one at a time on the main thread.
Queued commands run back-to-back without interleaving. No rollback on runtime errors; use WATCH for optimistic checks.
Multi-step logic (check then act) runs atomically on the server in one round trip. Keep it short: it blocks the server.
